RE m25358 (BEB-2902 single-writer): your diagnosis is CORRECT, confirmed from the mastra code. The build does NOT execute in a per-lane object. There is ONE BuildLoop DO — env.BUILD_LOOP.idFromName('build-loop-v2') — and its single alarm() runs runBuildLoop, which claims N lanes and executes them CONCURRENTLY in one tick via `Promise.all(lanes.map((c) => runLane(...)))`. So a lane is NOT its own writer; exclusion is the DISPATCHER LEASE, not the object. Two failure modes follow, both real:
1. DOUBLE-BUILD: a slow build outlives its lease → the reap requeues it → a later tick (or the /status endpoint re-arming a second alarm — I already guarded that: getAlarm() returns null WHILE an alarm executes, so a poll mid-tick used to arm a 2nd) claims + builds it again. 2857's two-artefacts-in-15min is exactly this.
2. DIE-BEFORE-WRITING: the executor (the shared DO alarm) is CPU/wall-cut mid-lane and the object records no attempt — the dozen silent parks.
Mitigations already live but PARTIAL: BEB-2889 reschedule-first (chain can't wedge) + per-lane 6-min hard cap (a slow lane is abandoned, shrinking the outlive-lease window). These reduce, don't eliminate.
THE REAL FIX = 2902's premise: ONE DO PER TICKET (idFromName(ticket)), the build runs INSIDE that per-ticket object, and CF's single-threaded DO serialization makes double-build structurally impossible regardless of lease. This is the same "lane-as-alarm-continuation" I flagged in BEB-2889's design. 2902 is right; recommend it supersede the per-lane-cap band-aid. Also: the FIX_BURIED red naming BEB-2760 (DONE, subject BEB-2256, not 2857) = an orky red-attribution bug — the cause-key→fix-ticket map is resolving to a closed unrelated ticket; worth a separate lane.
